title: Health literacy and self-management in long-term cancer survivors – Participatory development and evaluation of a digital, diversity-sensitive tool to promote health literacy
summary:
This project aims to develop and test a digital program that supports long-term cancer survivors in finding, understanding, and using health information to better manage their health and everyday life. The program will help users improve their health knowledge (health literacy) and self-management skills so they can make informed decisions and feel more confident in dealing with health-related challenges.
The digital program will be developed together with long-term survivors and patient advocates. Their ideas, experiences, and needs will be included from the very beginning. They will be involved as co-researchers and co-developers of the project. An advisory board made up of patient representatives and other experts will also help guide the process.
First, the team will look at existing support programs and identify what works well and what is missing or difficult to use. Then, in three group discussions (focus groups) with about 5–8 long-term survivors each, participants will share their needs and wishes for the digital program. These discussions will help make sure the program is useful and easy to understand for different people.
Based on this, the project team and co-developers will work with a software company to create a first version (prototype) of the digital program. This prototype will be tested in about 20 individual interviews. Based on the feedback, a more complete version (beta version) will be created.
Finally, the beta version will be tested in a larger study with 800 long-term survivors to find out how well the program is accepted and how helpful it is in improving health knowledge, confidence, and quality of life. Participants will be invited to take part through the networks of the project team and partner organizations, such as national cancer support groups.

interventions.name: Digital intervention to promote health literacy, self-efficacy expectations, health-related quality of life, and reduction of perceived stress

A content-reduced version ('control intervention') that provides only basic information on the topic. Assigning this reduced version to the control group helps prevent bias due to placebo and Hawthorne effects, and also allows for digital collection of outcomes and covariates within the control grou

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
A previous cancer diagnosis, willingness to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
No previous cancer diagnosis, no willingness to participate in the study
